summary: The note describes a growing local trend, since September 2023, of outdoor and green exercise in the city's parks and greenways. It covers the mental and physical benefits, free classes, running clubs, equipment-free workouts, fitness trails in community gardens, apps, adaptive programs, safety improvements, business impact, and healthcare collaboration. A 'Green Fit Fest' is planned for spring 2024.
one_line: Local residents have embraced outdoor and green exercise since September 2023, supported by city programs, businesses, apps, adaptive programs and community groups.
key_facts: Since September 2023 the community has seen a significant increase in people taking workouts outside.
Jessica Torres, a 42-year-old elementary school teacher, switched to green exercise through yoga sessions at Liberty Park after never being a gym person.
Studies as recent as October 2023 highlighted outdoor fitness benefits such as improved mood, increased energy levels, and reduced stress.
The City Council and local fitness groups collaborated on free community classes, from Tai Chi to boot camps, introduced in early November 2023.
Amara Singh, a local marathon runner, founded the 'Pace and Peace Running Crew,' whose weekly runs cater to all levels and use scenic routes.
Outdoor fitness spots with permanent pull-up bars and balance beams have appeared in parks like Maple Field, fostering a 'gym-free' culture.
Horticulturist Elena Rodriguez started a community garden on October 15, 2023 that incorporates fitness trails through vegetable plots and fruit trees.
The 'GreenFit Tracker' app launched in September 2023, letting users like Jamal Foster find outdoor workout spots, log activities and join virtual challenges.
In late September, non-profit 'Adapt and Achieve' introduced wheelchair-accessible fitness circuits at Community Park, praised by Paralympian Sarah Kim.
Well-lit pathways and designated exercise zones let Rebecca Li, a single mother, run after dusk.
Michael Chen, owner of 'Active Outdoors', saw a sales uptick around September 2023, coinciding with National Public Lands Day.
Dr. Nora Patel, a local physician, says partnering with fitness professionals supplements traditional medicine with green exercise.
The 'Green Fit Fest' is scheduled for spring 2024 as a celebration of outdoor exercise.
